constraints: Every spacing value — padding, margin, gap, row and panel height, column width — is a multiple of 8, at every level of the design. 4px is a permitted half-step; type, 1px borders and radii are exempt. Written up in DESIGN-RULES.md.
Panel and column positions are constants; content scrolls inside its own box rather than growing it; scroll gutters are reserved.
Nothing drifts, floats or animates on its own. Transitions are colour and opacity only, on direct interaction.
Every claim carries a credible reference with a link so it can be verified.
Summaries quote the source verbatim rather than paraphrasing it.

feedback.title: Tell the two picker shortcuts apart
feedback.quote: more distinct from each other
did: Each one is its own control

annual only and select all 13 were two runs of 10px small caps side by side and read as one string. Each now carries its own outline and 4/8px padding, so the 8px between them is a gap between two objects rather than a word space. Disabled dims the outline as well as the text.

feedback.title: A fitting icon for normal
feedback.quote: replace - with a fitting icon
did: The dash became a bar, and the bar was still just a mark. Normal is now the open circle the map already uses for an unflagged marker — marking it low or high is what adds the triangle. The three buttons now say below the range / in it / above it in the map’s own vocabulary rather than in three unrelated glyphs.

feedback.title: Component labels can be 10px
feedback.quote: these kind of titles can be 10 px, apply to all similar component texts
did: Picker title cut to one word
Panels you have had wrapped onto two lines beside its two shortcuts. It is Panels now — the rail already says whose bloodwork this is, and the chips say which ones are on.
The three map column titles, missed on the first pass

.map .colttl and .kbdhint both sit under a comment block, and the sweep that rewrote the rules read the comment as part of the selector — so the two most visible labels on the page were the two it skipped. Both are 10px now, and the check is no longer “does this selector match a list” but “is any mono rule still at 12px”, which answers zero.
A second tier, defined by what the text is

10px is now reserved for mono, uppercase, tracked text that names what is below it rather than being part of it: the three map column titles, panel group headers, the divider band, section kickers, the picker header and its two shortcuts, the quoted / ai-written tags, family headers, the keyboard hint. 36 rules in all. Anything sentence-case, or that carries meaning on its own — marker names, concern names, chips, buttons, body copy — stays at 12px.

10px labels sit on a 12px lead rather than the 16px content lead, which is what makes them read as a signpost. That also bought back rows: at 1280×720 the marker column now shows 21 of 26 markers individually where it showed 19.

§1b now states the test rather than a list: a label may be quieter than what it points at; if it is sentence-case or is content in its own right, it is not one of these. Scale is 10 / 12 / 16 / 18 / 20.

feedback.title: Left panel header, same shape as the right
feedback.quote: reformat the left panel title to match the right panel title section
did: The rail header was a serif h1 and a paragraph; the detail panel was a mono kicker, a serif title and a short line, in a 96px box. Both are now the second thing: YOUR BLOODWORK / Start with your annual panel / Mark anything that came back low or high. The two panels are in register because they are the same object, not because two sets of numbers were matched up.
Both kicker lines now sit on the same baseline as the map’s three column titles — one line across the whole screen.

feedback.title: 12px floor, 2px steps, no decoration
feedback.quote: the smallest font size on the page shouldn’t be smaller than 12px, each size up is 2x pixels. remove unnecessary styling
did: The page had thirteen sizes between 8px and 19px. It now has four — 12, 16, 18, 20 — and 12px is the floor everywhere, including every label on the map. The map’s line height is 16px and its shortest row is 16px.
The map no longer scales its type

The two solvers that stepped the type from 12px down to 8px to make a column fit are gone, and with them the whole class of bug where a column was measured at one size and drawn at another. Type size is now a constant, not a variable.
What absorbs a small window instead

Content, and it says so. A marker panel with nothing marked folds to one row with its true count; the concern column places what fits and the divider band carries the rest — 29 concerns no panel marker can reach · add any of them in the panel, which is exactly where they are. At 1920×1080 all 47 concerns are listed; at 900px tall, the 18 the panel reaches are listed and the other 29 are counted.
Truncation is now gone from the map entirely
The last three line-caps — panel group headers, the divider band, and the rail’s marker names — wrapped instead. No ellipsis is produced anywhere on the page.
Drop shadows, background blur and translucent panel fills are gone; a panel is a white box with a 1px border. Inline font-size overrides in the SVG are gone too — size lives in one CSS rule.
feedback.open: The 12px floor costs rows. At 1280×720 with the annual panel selected, one of the three panels folds; at that size the old build showed all 26 markers at 8px.

feedback.title: An icon for normal
feedback.quote: use an icon for normal
did: A drawn bar, not a dash character

Low and high are solid triangles; normal was an en-dash borrowed from the type. It is now a bar drawn at the same optical weight — 9×2px, 1px radius — so the three states read as one set. It inherits the button’s colour, so the selected state needs no separate rule.

feedback.title: Still not bottom aligned
feedback.quote: still not bottom aligned
did: The first attempt computed the kicker’s baseline from padding and line-height. That cannot be right in general: where a baseline falls inside a line box depends on the font’s own ascent and descent, which CSS does not expose. The kicker’s box is now measured against the stage at render time.
Centre to centre, not baseline to baseline

An SVG y is a baseline; a CSS box is not. Rather than convert between them and guess the metrics, the column titles are set dominant-baseline:central and aligned centre to centre. They are the same size and face as the kicker, so equal centres are equal baselines.
Re-applied after the panel is drawn

The map is drawn before the detail panel, so on the first paint there was no kicker to measure. The measured y is re-applied once the panel has content — it moves three text nodes and touches nothing else.

feedback.title: Both runs of dots, one spacing
feedback.quote: the 2 sets of dots should have the same spacing in between
did: Marker dot to concern dot, and concern out-dot to follow-up dot, are both exactly one 40px column gap — so the two runs of edges span the same distance. Verified at four window sizes: 40.0 and 40.0 at every one.

feedback.title: One baseline for the titles, equal thirds for the columns
feedback.quote: align the text to [concern exposure and lifestyle] - bottom aligned. make all titles shorter, so [would follow up] section have wider column to make all 3 columns and gaps the same
did: The three column titles now sit on the same baseline as the detail panel’s kicker line. That needed the panel’s own header pinned to the top of its box instead of centred in it — centred text moves with its content, so there was no stable line to align to.

YOUR ANNUAL PANEL · 26 → YOUR PANEL · 26, WHAT THEY CAN POINT AT · 47 → CAN POINT AT · 47, WOULD FOLLOW IT UP → WOULD FOLLOW UP. A heading competes with the names below it for the same width, and the names need it more.

The columns were 21.5% / 38% / 22.5% of the free width with uneven gaps. They are now exact thirds separated by one 40px gap. At 1600px that takes the marker column from 101px of label width to 250px and the follow-up column from 191px to 261px — enough that no marker name wraps at any tested window size.

feedback.title: Even spacing for each column
feedback.quote: even spacing for each column
did: Spare height shared equally, not in proportion

Rows differ in height because names now wrap, and the leftover height was being shared in proportion to each row — so a two-line row got twice the breathing room of a one-line one and the column read as ragged. The same number of pixels is now added to every row, which makes the gap between one name and the next a constant down the whole column. Measured: gap spread is 0.1px in all three columns at four window sizes.
One measured size, not one drawn size

A second cause: the marker column was measured at 12px and drawn at 11px, because the shared type size is the smaller of the two columns and was settled after the marker column had already budgeted its rows. The concern column is now solved first, the marker column is capped at that size, and the concern column re-solves if the marker column steps down further — so what is measured is what is drawn.

feedback.title: Text must respect the panel gutter, and wrap
feedback.quote: again, respect the padding between text and right panel, put in multiple rows of text if needed, put in rule and apply to all text and relationship to panels
did: The real cause was an unbreakable name

The column width already reserved the 16px gutter. What broke it was wrap(), which could only break at spaces — so Gamma glutamyl transferase.macromolecular was one token and ran straight under the detail panel. It is now broken at a natural boundary (. + / - ,) or hard if there is none.
Names wrap to as many rows as they need

The three-line cap with an ellipsis is gone from the follow-up column, and the marker and concern columns — which were capped at two lines and one clipped line respectively — now wrap freely. Row heights are measured from the wrapped result, so nothing collides.
Type size is spent before content is
When a column will not fit, the type steps down from 12px to the 8px floor first. Only then does a panel fold. Truncation is no longer a step in that sequence anywhere in the map.
Written into the rules and checked

New design rules: text never runs under a panel (§6) and even spacing within a column (§5b). The regression measures the widest label’s right edge against the panel gutter at six window sizes and the leftmost label against the rail at five — all clear.

feedback.title: A reset and a select-all for the panel picker
feedback.quote: it’s kinda annoying to toggle on and off each one, can we have a reset button to annual? and a select all?
did: Two shortcuts on the picker header

annual only resets to the routine checkup; select all 13 turns on the whole library. They hold their place whatever the state — when the selection already matches, the button dims rather than disappearing, so the header never reflows.

All 13 panels is 68 markers, which at 900px gave each row 5px — unreadable. A panel with nothing marked in it now folds to one row carrying its true count, with its edges bundled there and every one of its markers still listed in the rail. A panel you have marked never folds, and the annual panel on its own is never folded at any window size.

feedback.title: The whole row is the button
feedback.quote: make entire row clickable, no need to underscore, remove top and bottom border when row is selected
did: The follow-up row carries data-test itself instead of wrapping a link, so the whole row — name, unit chip, quoted/ai-written tag and the padding around them — responds to the click. The name inside is now a span, not a button.
text-decoration removed. The row is visibly interactive from its hover fill; an underline on top of that is a second signal for the same thing.
No rule on a selected row
A selected row is a fill, not a fill plus two hairlines: .mrow.sel drops to border-color:transparent and a selected follow-up row hides its own bottom rule and the next row’s top.

feedback.title: Blue edges read heavier than orange
feedback.quote: why is blue line so much thicker? make it same weight as the orange
did: One weight for every marked edge

The cause was .edge.hot, which pushed a selected or hovered edge to 2.6px while a marked-low or marked-high edge stayed at 1.6px — so the teal selection always looked thicker than the orange marks. Every marked edge is now 1.6px and .hot raises opacity only.
Written into the design rules: emphasis in the map is carried by colour and opacity. Line weight encodes nothing, so changing state never changes the shape of the drawing.

feedback.title: Accept lab-directory sourcing; fix the empty BMP; one annual toggle
feedback.quote: yes accept, also there’s nothing showing under basic metabolic panel, fix it. and have annual blood panel be in one toggle
did: With lab-directory sourcing accepted, the library grows from 8 panels to 13: Anemia Profile B (Labcorp, 7 of 7 components mapped), Testicular Function Profile I (Labcorp, 4 of 4), ReproSURE ovarian reserve (Labcorp, 3 of 3), Autoimmune and Inflammation Marker Panel (Quest, 4 of 7) and Hepatocellular Carcinoma Tumor Marker Panel (ARUP, 1 of 3). 68 markers in total.
Labcorp’s Celiac Antibodies Profile was investigated and not added: none of its four components exist in the 6,192-row catalogue, so the panel would have been four not carried rows and nothing else.

Real bug, and a structural one. BMP is a strict subset of the CMP, and a marker shared by two selected panels is listed once under the first — so with the annual panel on, BMP had a header and zero rows. The header now states where its markers went (all also above), in the rail and in the map, and the space that line takes is measured rather than borrowed from the padding.

CBC, CMP and lipids carry a shared grp and the picker renders one Annual panel chip for all three — nobody has had a CMP without the rest of the checkup. The marker column keeps the three sub-headings, so what came from where is still legible.
feedback.open: Eight components across the thyroid, inflammation and HCC panels are not in the catalogue and stay marked as such.

feedback.title: More panels to explore beyond the annual routine
feedback.quote: now looking at blood tests by panel grouping seems manageable, can we create more panels apart from annual panel for ppl to explore? such as cancer panel (Galleri), thyroid panels, hormone panels, autoimmune panels etc.
quotes: now looking at blood tests by panel grouping seems manageable, can we create more panels apart from annual panel for ppl to explore? such as cancer panel (Galleri), thyroid panels, hormone panels, autoimmune panels etc.
search for them and map with our database, here are some sources I can find already: kidshealth.org / my.clevelandclinic.org
did: Added Basic Metabolic Panel, Liver function panel and Iron studies from MedlinePlus, and Thyroid panel and ENA panel from Cleveland Clinic — each with a verbatim description and component list, joining the three that were already there. 46 markers in total.

Every component is matched to a real catalogue row by LOINC analyte name, source-quoted rows preferred. All six ENA antibodies, all four iron studies and GGT, LDH and PT/INR for the liver panel are present.

Eight panels is too many for tabs and they are not mutually exclusive — someone can have had a CMP and a thyroid panel — so the rail carries a multi-select picker. Markers shared by two selected panels are listed once, under the first.
Three components we do not carry

The thyroid panel's TPO antibodies, thyroglobulin antibodies and TSI are not in the 6,192-row catalogue. They are shown in the panel marked not carried rather than quietly dropped — a panel we cannot fully model is itself worth knowing about.
Header, footer and the personal-concern layer all recompute: 3 of 8 panels reaches 18 of 47 concerns; all 8 reaches 22.

Not added, and it should not be. MedlinePlus has no page on it — a direct search returns nothing — and it is not structurally a panel: it is a single methylation-based cfDNA assay returning one signal-detected result, not a list of markers you could mark low or high.

MedlinePlus links ~18 individual hormone tests but names no panel; Cleveland Clinic's hormone-panel slug is dead. Only commercial lab-shopping sites publish one, which is below our sourcing bar. The thyroid panel covers part of the ground.
Tumour markers are ordered one at a time against a particular cancer — both MedlinePlus and Cleveland Clinic present them as a category, not a bundle. There is no panel to add.
feedback.open: Hormone, inflammation and cancer panels have no citable component list from a non-commercial source. The options are to accept lab-directory sourcing (Labcorp, Quest, ARUP publish named panel contents, and the catalogue already flags such rows differently) or to leave those areas to the concern column, which already reaches them.

feedback.title: Arrows select; the dashed state belongs to Tab
feedback.quote: and when arrow keys pressed, it acts as a click, so directly show the selected panel. the dash line status is only used when tab is pressed, when hovering, the current status is good
did: Arrows now act like a click
They move and select, so the detail panel follows as you go rather than needing Enter. Same code path as a mouse click, so a row reached by arrow looks identical to one reached by pointer.

Tab steps a dashed preview through every row in all three columns without changing the selection; Shift+Tab goes back; Enter commits whatever the preview is on. Focus records how it was moved, so the two never mix.
The ? panel now describes arrows as selecting and Tab as previewing.

feedback.title: Fixed height for the follow-up section; a click is a fill, not a dashed ring
feedback.quote: use this height as fixed default for what would follow it up section
quotes: use this height as fixed default for what would follow it up section
when mouse clicked, it shouldn’t be the dashed line status, should be filled color no border status
did: The section was sizing to its content, so the panel changed shape between concerns — 2 families or 12 gave very different layouts. It now holds a fixed 384px (8×48) and scrolls inside, capped at 52% of the panel so a short window stays sane. Expanding still hands it the remaining space.
A click is a fill, not an outline

The dashed ring is a keyboard focus affordance and was appearing on mouse clicks too. Focus now records how it was moved: clicking gives the solid filled row with no border, arrow keys give the dashed ring. Verified both ways in both the map and the rail.

feedback.title: Full names with constant padding, doubled quote mark, keyboard resumes from the last click
feedback.quote: show full name, put in rule, allow multiple rows if needed. each test will have the same paddings around regardless how many rows of the name it takes
quotes: show full name, put in rule, allow multiple rows if needed. each test will have the same paddings around regardless how many rows of the name it takes
remove the one additional quotation mark
when using shortcuts on keyboard, esp arrow keys, start navigation based on where the last click was, not from default beginning
did: Full names on the map, never cut
Follow-up entries wrap to up to three lines instead of ending in an ellipsis. Zero truncated at every width tested.
Constant padding whatever the line count
Each entry carries exactly 8px above and below whether its name takes one line or three — the row grows, the padding does not. Measured identical across a mixed one- and two-line block.

DESIGN-RULES.md §4 now states it: names are shown in full and wrap rather than truncate; padding is constant regardless of line count so rows in a list may legitimately differ in height; long lists are grouped rather than cut, with the true count on every header.

Descriptions arrive from the catalogue already wrapped in quotes and are rendered in a <q> element, which adds its own. The strip only handled straight quotes, so curly ones came through and doubled up. Now every flavour is stripped at build time.
Keyboard resumes from the last click

Clicking a marker, a concern, a follow-up test or a low/high toggle now moves the keyboard focus to that item, so the arrow keys carry on from where you were rather than restarting at the top of the first column.

feedback.title: Group the long lists, dock the panels, 12px everywhere, full-row highlights
feedback.quote: any follow up more than 10 are too overwhelming, how can we simplify the guide without losing info?
quotes: any follow up more than 10 are too overwhelming, how can we simplify the guide without losing info?
fully left and right anchor the panels to reduce empty space, same as the bottom panel
use only 12 px for all at same height
the highlight should be the entire row, fix the framework to allow it, apply to all similar components
did: What the long tail actually is

23 of 47 concerns carry more than 40 markers. But medication monitoring, the worst at 378, has 372 of them in one family, and by the catalogue's own ordering tier only 1 is commonly ordered against 117 specialist and 260 rarely ordered. The tail is not variety, it is obscure variants.

The list now opens as family headers carrying their true total, with only the commonly-ordered markers shown under each. Medication monitoring reads as 4 rows instead of 378. Every family opens on click, and nothing is dropped — the counts state exactly what is behind each header.
Panels docked to the window edges
Rail, detail and footer sit flush to their edges with square outer corners; the 16px now lives only between a panel and the map, which hands the map back 32px of width and 32 of height.

Every label in every column is 12px Open Sans regular on a uniform row height. 12px holds from about 875px of window height upward; below that it steps down rather than letting rows collide, which is the only case where it is not exactly 12.

Rows now carry their own horizontal padding and cancel their container's with a negative margin, so a hover or a selection covers the whole row edge to edge. Applied to every row-like component — marker rows, follow-up rows, family headers and the why-list — not just the one that showed the problem.
feedback.open: The map's third column still draws individual markers rather than families; grouping it was agreed but is the next step.

feedback.title: Divider alignment, wrapped concern names, one type style
feedback.quote: use the same text style as the left column, tell me the size and typography
quotes: align 29 with heart and cholesterol, use the same bottom spacing [what they can point at] has to [29 concerns no panel marker can reach]
these names are still missing full name, put in multiple rows if needed
use the same text style as the left column, tell me the size and typography
did: Divider aligned to the concern names
It was starting at the dot rather than the label, 21px left of Heart & cholesterol. Both now start at the same x.
Same bottom spacing as a column header
Column headers sit 16px above their first row; the divider band now closes 16px after its last baseline, with the rule halfway through. Measured identical at every width.
Concern rows can be two lines

Row heights are no longer uniform — a name that will not fit on one line gets a taller row and the height is borrowed from the rest of the column. The wrapping decision always reserves room for the marker-count chip, so nothing reflows when you mark a marker.

Narrowing the column makes more names wrap, which needs height, which can force the type down, which changes the wrapping again. Settled by iteration instead of a fixed multiplier, with a one-line truncated fallback if two lines cannot fit at the 8px floor — so rows can never run past the bottom of the map.
One type style across all three columns

Open Sans regular at a single size chosen per render from the tightest column budget — markers, concerns and follow-ups always match. State is carried by colour alone; the bold on live concerns and marked markers is gone, matching the rule already applied to the dots.

feedback.title: Respect the side panels on a narrow screen
feedback.quote: when screen’s smaller, respect the space taken by the side panels and show texts around it, the [complete blood count, comprehensive metabolic panel, and cholesterol lipid panel] are too close or covered by the panel right now, make them flexible to be on multiple rows as long as we keep same padding between panel and text always
did: The map only subtracted the rail’s width when the window was wider than 1080px — but the rail is always on screen; it is the detail panel and footer that get dropped. Below 1080 the marker column was being laid out from the window edge, so it ran under the rail.

The left boundary now always allows for it, and the padding between any panel and the nearest text is a constant 16px on every edge at every size. Verified from 860px to 2560px wide: the leftmost text never crosses the rail.

Complete blood count, comprehensive metabolic panel and cholesterol / lipid panel wrap to as many lines as the column needs — 4 lines across the three groups at 1512px, 7 at 860px — instead of running under the panel.
Space they take is measured, not assumed
The header block height is computed from the wrapped line count, so the marker rows are laid out around it. Previously a fixed 15px was reserved regardless.

feedback.title: Divider: more air on top, balanced, wrapping
feedback.quote: more space on top, align text with top and bottom, put in multiple rows if needed
did: It was running past the column

29 concerns no panel marker can reach was a single unwrapped line, so can reach fell off the right edge below about 1440px. It now wraps on word boundaries to fit the column — one line to 1440, two below that, never truncated.
Height is computed from the number of wrapped lines rather than fixed, so a two-line divider gets a taller band instead of crowding.

24px above the first baseline and 16px below the rule — the extra 8 on top pays for the cap height, so the white space reads as equal. Measured: ~30px above, ~34px below, against 21/21 before and a visibly tighter top.

feedback.title: Marker column alignment, arrow gutter, and the divider as a header
feedback.quote: reserve space on the left of dot for arrow icons, right align all texts including the subheaders, put in multiple rows if needed
quotes: reserve space on the left of dot for arrow icons, right align all texts including the subheaders, put in multiple rows if needed
more space around this title, put in the same style as [what they can point at], remove the arrow
did: The ▼▲ was appended to the label text, so marking a marker pushed its name left. It now sits in a reserved 16px slot between the label edge and the dot — verified that every label x is identical before and after marking.
One right edge for the whole column

Labels and the panel sub-headers (complete blood count, comprehensive metabolic panel, cholesterol / lipid panel) are all right-aligned to the same line, 24px left of the dot. The sub-headers were left-aligned against the opposite edge.
Losing 24px to the gutter is absorbed by the existing word-wrap; no marker name is truncated down to 1280px, and only one is at 1200.
Divider reads as a section header

29 concerns no panel marker can reach now uses the same style as what they can point at, with the arrow dropped and the band opened from 17px to 55px — 21px of clearance above the label and below the rule.

feedback.title: Repeated recommendations, test drill-in, keyboard, full names, matching dots
feedback.quote: why would some returned content have bunch of repeated test recommendations?
quotes: why would some returned content have bunch of repeated test recommendations?
give keyboard shortcuts (arrow keys to go down up the list, left right the columns etc.) to navigate the page better
click on each of them should lead to the curated right panel of the test details
instead of not showing the rest name using [...], put full names on two rows if needed
after clicking on a test, the right panel shows the test details while the test is highlighted under [would follow it up] with the rest content, not disappearing
dots should be in the same size and style
did: The repeats were real, and were ours

LOINC carries one code per unit, specimen and method, so Lead [Presence] in Blood, Lead [Mass/volume] in Blood and Lead [Moles/volume] in Blood are three codes for one test. Truncating the name at the first bracket collapsed them into a list that read Lead, Lead, Lead. 41% of carried rows were duplicate labels.

Rows are grouped by the thing measured — bracket, trailing in <specimen> and by <method> all stripped, since LOINC often puts the specimen in bare text. Best-ranked row per analyte kept, the rest counted as a ×n chip. Heavy metals: 53 rows → 9 markers. Smoking: 21 → 4.
Counts now say which is which
Headers and tooltips report distinct markers; the note reports both — all 9 markers carried here · from 53 LOINC rows.

↑↓ within a column, ←→ between them, Home/End, Enter to select, L/N/H to mark the focused marker, X to add a concern, E to expand, R to reset, Esc to clear, ? for the shortcut sheet. Crossing columns follows the edges, not the row order: right from a marker lands on the first concern it points at, left from a concern lands on the first marker pointing at it.
Click a test for its own panel

Follow-ups are clickable from the list, the map and the keyboard. The panel shows what it measures with its source and verify link, any sourced relationship notes, and chips for every concern it is tagged to.

Selecting a test used to null the open concern, so the whole third column disappeared. The parent concern now stays open, the map keeps its rows, and the row highlights in place in the panel — including when it sits past the collapsed cut-off.

Labels wrap on word boundaries instead of truncating. The over-reserved right margin in the concern column was reclaimed, so every concern name now fits on one line down to 1366px wide. Type tightens when a follow-up wraps so both lines clear the 24px pitch.
All four kinds of dot were different sizes. Now a single 5px radius across all three columns, with state carried by fill and stroke colour rather than geometry.
feedback.open: The file is 527 KB, up from 230, because each carried marker now brings its description so the test panel has something to show.

feedback.title: Centre the low/norm/high labels over their pill segments
feedback.quote: align the low norm high to the center of each pill option
did: The header sat 8px right of the pill it labels. The marker list reserves an 8px scrollbar gutter that the header, sitting outside the scroll area, does not — so identical 16px padding on both put them out of register.
Right padding 16 → 24, matching the list’s 8px gutter plus 8px row padding. Both columns now end at panel − 24.
Each label centred on its own segment
The label row is a 3-column grid matching the pill’s, with each label a block centred in its 24px cell rather than centred as one run of text.
NORM and HIGH were running together: 9px type with .06em tracking is ~22.4px in a 24px cell. Dropped to 8.5px with no tracking — 20.4px, leaving clear gutters.

feedback.title: Glyph pill, and anchor the follow-up list at the bottom
feedback.quote: since we have labels, no need to show words again in the pill, we can use other visual cues to indicate low and high, and save some space on pill design
quotes: since we have labels, no need to show words again in the pill, we can use other visual cues to indicate low and high, and save some space on pill design
always anchor this section in full (before expanding) at the bottom of the right panel

▼ and ▲ are the same marks already used on flagged markers in the map, so the two views read the same way.
Three 24px segments. The 24px saved goes back to the marker-name column, which now fits Aspartate aminotransferase without truncating.
Follow-up list anchored to the bottom
margin-top:auto pins it to the foot of the panel, and it sizes to its content so all eight rows, the expander and the note show in full without scrolling.
Expanding flips it to the flexible section
Collapsed it is fixed-height and unscrolled; expanded to 40 it takes the remaining space and scrolls inside itself. The relationship notes above take whatever is left, with a 176px floor.
8 drawn on the map · top 40 of 386 carried here over tagged to this concern and ranked — not a confirmed diagnostic sequence, so the honesty survives without eating the rows.
72, 24, 8 and 4 throughout. Re-audited: zero off-grid spacing.

feedback.title: Give the relationship notes more room by default
feedback.quote: give more space for this section by default
did: Section is no longer a fixed 184px box
“How these connect” now flexes. It takes the larger share of whatever height is left after the header and the explanation — flex:1.6 against flex:1 for the follow-up list — with a 264px floor.
Two full notes visible by default
At a 880px-tall window the section clears roughly 300px, enough for two complete quote cards instead of one and a clipped second.
Card spacing 16px → 24px, with the last card’s margin removed so the section does not end on dead space.

feedback.title: An atlas of blood, not another lab viewer
feedback.quote: What we don't have is a model of the blood system itself. We don't know what other markers surround a result, what hasn't been measured, what should be measured next, or how biomarkers relate to one another across physiology.
quotes: We already have good tools for seeing individual blood tests—and simple trends over time.

Imagine a map instead of a list. Every blood marker exists within networks: inflammation, immunity, kidney function, metabolism, liver health, hormones, nutrition, coagulation, cancer, infection, genetics, and more. We need the “solar system” of blood markers, not isolated planets.
The most valuable information may be what's missing. Which tests have never been ordered? Which families of tests are incomplete? … Missing data is itself clinical information.
This is fundamentally a decision-space design problem.

More data isn't the problem. Claude Shannon taught us that information reduces uncertainty. The challenge is designing interfaces that transform more information into better decisions instead of more confusion.

The issue isn't the data itself. The problem is that we haven't designed an effective way for clinicians and patients to navigate it—to surface what's important, summarize the signals, expose the gaps, and reveal the relationships.
The product isn't another lab viewer. It's a decision engine.

The goal isn't simply to display blood work. It's to make the invisible structure of human physiology visible enough that clinicians and patients can ask better questions, order better tests, and make better decisions.
did: A map instead of a list
The atlas screen shows all 17 families as a packed map sized by what is inside them, replacing a landing page whose only promise was 6,192 rows.
The hero leads with 26 of 6,192 — what a routine annual panel measures against what is measurable. The stat strip shows three gaps instead of three totals.
The gap map takes what you have had drawn and returns per-family coverage. 14 of 17 families are untouched by a standard annual panel.
All six are on the landing as navigation, each honestly labelled. Two work; two are prototypes; one is evidenced for three panels only; one is not built.
Only the three routine panels are modelled as sets. Nothing else in the catalogue is grouped by “ordered together”.
Not built, and deliberately not faked. Only 6 of 6,192 markers carry a link to another family, so the map draws no edges and says so.
Blocked on the same missing relationship layer. The one worked example (iron-deficiency anemia) is hand-authored in condition-lens.html.
Screen-then-confirm exists as a prototype for one condition, not as a general capability.
Not built. Named as not built on the landing rather than quietly omitted.
What each biomarker means, with evidence
All 6,192 carry a description and a link, but only 216 are quoted from a named authority; 5,976 were AI-written from the LOINC name. The ratio is on the front door.
feedback.open: The relationship layer is the blocker for three of the points above. The fix is two small additions alongside tests — a sets array for “these are ordered together” and an edges array for reflex links like low MCV → ferritin — each carrying its own quoted or reasoned source. Scoped in §5 of INDEX-REFINEMENT.md. Until it exists, any marker-level ripple view would be drawing edges that are not in the data.

changes: Follow-ups centred on their concern row at a 24px pitch, with a tick on the anchor row. They were previously centred in the column, which is why they started mid-page.
Pill rebuilt on the 8px system — 24px tall, 8px padding per segment, 96px column, 32px rows. No more clipped words.
Non-scrolling column header labels the marker column and the three toggle segments.
Rail widened to 320px (8×40) so the padded pill does not squeeze the marker names.
Source badge moved off the map into the detail list and tooltip, so each follow-up is one line and the block stays short enough to centre.
Verified at six window sizes: zero label overlaps, zero overflow, out-dots clear of text, 92–96% width and 99–100% height in use.
versions.note: Centring clamps for concerns in the top ~130px, where a centred block would run off the canvas. Unavoidable; the anchor tick keeps the relationship readable.

versions.title: Ripple atlas — right-side connectors
versions.summary: Concern rows gain a second connector dot on their right edge, and the follow-up edges leave from there instead of sweeping back across the label text.
changes: 47 right-hand connector dots, one per concern row, at the right edge of the column.
Follow-up edges originate at the out-dot rather than the left-hand dot, so no curve crosses a label.
The out-dot is quiet grey until its row is the one feeding the third column, then warm and filled.
Marker-count chip moved inboard to clear the new dot; label clip widths re-measured.
Verified at six window sizes: zero label overlaps, zero overflow, out-dots clear of all text.
versions.note: Only the concern column changed. Markers already had their dot on the outgoing side, and follow-up tests already had theirs on the incoming side.

versions.title: Ripple atlas — three columns
versions.summary: Static, deterministic, and dense: panel markers, concerns and follow-up tests as three fixed columns filling the whole canvas. No physics, no drift, no animation.
changes: Force simulation deleted. Layout is a pure function of state and window size.
Three fixed columns — 26 panel markers grouped by CBC / CMP / lipid, all 47 concerns, and the follow-up tests for whichever concern is open.
Every row is labelled. Full marker names, full concern names, no culling.
Barycentre ordering puts each concern beside the markers that point at it, so edges run flat rather than crossing.
A drawn divider separates the 18 concerns the annual panel can reach from the 29 it cannot.
Type scales with row height and clips to its column: zero label overlaps and zero overflow at 1200×700 through 2560×1400.
Space used: 99–100% of the height, 91–96% of the width.
versions.note: Supersedes both v2.0 (fixed rings) and v2.1 (force layout). The rail, detail panel and the 29 sourced relationship notes are unchanged.

versions.title: Ripple atlas — organic layout
versions.summary: The ripple map stops being a fixed ring and becomes a live force simulation: nodes float, live concerns pull inward, dormant ones drift to the edge, and labels are placed only where they fit.
changes: Force simulation replaces the fixed rings. A radial band per role, concerns sprung toward the markers that implicate them, universal repulsion, hard collision correction, and a boundary that keeps every node out of the panels.
Live concerns come forward, dormant ones recede. The 47 concerns no longer each hold a permanent ring slot — the ones in play grow and move inward where there is room to label them.

Greedy label placement. Labels are sorted by importance and take the first of four candidate positions that collides with nothing. Zero label overlaps at 1200×700 through 1920×1080, in every interaction state.
Elliptical bands so the layout fills a wide rectangle instead of inscribing a circle in it.
Ambient drift — per-node phase, slow breathing motion, disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
Flowing dash on live edges so the ripple visibly travels outward from a marker you flag.
Node overlaps: zero once settled, at every size tested.
versions.note: Motion is confined to the map canvas. The rails, detail slots and scroll gutters stay fixed, so this does not undo the no-shift guarantee from v2.0.

versions.title: Ripple atlas
versions.summary: A different route into the atlas: start from the 26 markers of a routine annual panel, mark what came back abnormal, and watch the ripple spread into concerns and the tests that would follow them up.
changes: Three concentric rings. Inner: the 26 annual-panel markers, grouped by CBC / CMP / lipid. Middle: all 47 concerns, each holding a permanent slot. Outer: the follow-up tests for whichever concern is open.
Mark low or high on any panel marker and the concerns it can represent light up, with edges coloured by direction.
29 sourced relationship notes — every one a verbatim MedlinePlus (NIH) quote with a verify link, re-checked against the source pages after authoring.
Personal concern layer. The 29 concerns a routine panel cannot reach can be added by hand; one that no panel marker touches says so outright.

Nothing moves. Ring geometry is computed once per window size and cached; interactions change colour and opacity only. Scroll areas reserve their gutters. Verified by diffing every circle coordinate across marking, selecting and adding.
Marker radius derived from the ring chord, so the 26 inner circles cannot overlap at any window size. Checked at 1200×700 through 1920×1080.
95 KB standalone — no 6,192-row table, so it loads instantly.
versions.note: This is an alternative to the v1.1 family atlas, not a replacement. v1.1 maps the whole catalogue by family; v2.0 starts from what you have actually had done. Both are candidates.

versions.title: Atlas cockpit — fixed panels
versions.summary: The atlas stops being a scrolling page and becomes a fixed cockpit: the map fills the viewport, everything else floats above it, nothing ever reflows.
changes: Nothing scrolls or resizes. The stage is fixed; panels are absolutely positioned and hold their dimensions. Anything that could overflow scrolls inside its own box instead of growing.
Map is the ground plane. It fills the viewport behind four floating glass panels — controls and family index on the left, detail on the right, legend and the honesty line along the bottom.
Circles never jump. Positions are packed once per stage size and cached; toggling shade or re-ordering the index only re-paints colour. Verified by diffing circle coordinates across a shade toggle.

Packing is area-conserving — circles scale to fill ~46% of whatever space the panels leave, so the map uses the room it has at any window size. Panel footprints are measured, not guessed, so no circle hides under a panel.
Detail panel is always mounted at a fixed size. With nothing selected it shows the whole-atlas summary; selecting a family swaps the content without changing the box.
Drill-in is an overlay sheet that fades over the map — every marker in the family, filterable, each linking to its LOINC record. Esc or the scrim closes it.
Index and map cross-highlight on hover; clicking either selects, clicking again deselects.
No dimming of unselected families. The shape of what is unmeasured is the point of the map, so it stays readable while you inspect one family.
versions.note: The family-card grid from v1.0 is gone — the index rail and detail panel replace it. Landing and gap map are unchanged.

versions.title: Atlas rebuild
versions.summary: Landing reframed from a navigation question into a claim, plus two new screens: a gap map and a family atlas.
changes: Hero states the thesis. “Where do you want to start?” becomes “There are 6,192 things that can be measured in your blood. A routine annual checkup measures 26.”

Stat strip shows gaps, not totals. The volume pair (6,192 tests · 17 body systems) is replaced by 26 of 6,192 in a routine panel, 1,602 markers no symptom reaches, and 4 of 17 families with no quoted source.
New gap map (#cxGaps) — mark the panels you’ve had, search in individual markers, see per-family coverage. Persists to localStorage.
New family atlas (#cxAtlas) — 17 family cards, shade by routine-panel or source coverage, sort by size / least covered / A–Z.
Six-question spine on the landing, each labelled built / prototype / partial / not built.
Family map generated from the payload by deterministic circle packing. No edges drawn, because only 6 of 6,192 markers carry a link to another family.
Honesty band — 216 quoted entries vs 5,976 AI-written, with source names read out of the data.
Fixed two bugs found in testing: [].slice.call() on a Set returns empty, which had silently broken the added-markers list and localStorage persistence.
versions.note: Every figure is computed from the payload at load, so the copy cannot drift from the dataset. Regenerate with pipeline/build_v2.py.

versions.title: Free-text symptom search
versions.summary: The last state of the original dashboard before the atlas rebuild. This is the roll-back target if the atlas goes wrong.
changes: Free-text search on the condition explorer home (cxFeelSearch) with fuzzy matching into concern chips.
“Search all tests” escape hatch from the search results into the table view.
Feedback link added to the dashboard header.
Blood-fill animation on the landing figure retuned (cxrise 120px → 185px).
versions.note: These edits were uncommitted when the atlas work began; committed as their own milestone so this exact state stays recoverable.

versions.title: Polished landing and table toolbar
versions.summary: Visual pass on the two-door landing and usability work on the all-tests table.
changes: Landing figure with the blood-fill mask, animated leader lines to each route card, and live card stats read from the dataset.
Per-system mini bar chart on the “Explore all tests” card.
Table toolbar: expand all, collapse all, back to top, and a sticky toolbar dock.
Rollup system bar with legend in the dashboard header.

versions.title: Condition explorer prototype
versions.summary: The biggest single change in the project's history: conditions become a first-class object sitting between symptoms and tests.
changes: Route landing (#cxRoute) with two doors — start from how you feel, or explore all tests.
Condition explorer (#cxApp): symptom → candidate conditions → condition lens.
Condition lens with ripple diagram, “have you had this?” checklist, path-to-diagnosis track and a locked miniDx card.
All-tests table view with name / system / source filters.
Added condition-lens.html, IMPROVEMENT-PLAN.md and the pipeline/ source files.
versions.note: This is the version IMPROVEMENT-PLAN.md was written against.

versions.title: Initial dashboard
versions.summary: The original concern-in, test-list-out tool. No conditions, no landing page, no table view.
changes: 6,192-test catalogue with the concern picker and age / sex / life-stage / medication filters.
Rollup stat strip and callouts.
“Worth asking your doctor about” ranking, and annual-panel coverage against what sits outside it.
Source-quoted vs AI-generated badges throughout.
